artworks.title: Clio, Muse of History
artworks.description: Part of Charles Meynier's Neoclassical cycle of Apollo and the Muses, now in the Cleveland Museum of Art, this canvas personifies Kleio, the Muse of history, as a serene young woman seated against a sweeping landscape. She rests an open scroll on her knee and turns toward a stone slab inscribed with names, her gaze fixed on the act of recording the past. The open roll and the chest of papyri at her side render her traditional attributes — the keeper of memory who, as Hesiod sang in the Theogony, was born to Mnemosyne and so gives deeds their immortality in the written word.

artworks.title: Clio
artworks.description: Painted in 1632 for a patron connected to the Capponi family, Artemisia Gentileschi's Baroque allegory casts the Muse of history as a commanding figure who holds the trumpet of fame in one hand and an open book in the other, a laurel wreath crowning her head. The trumpet proclaims renown across the ages while the book preserves it, embodying Clio's role as the Muse whose office is to make great deeds outlast death. Gentileschi signed and dated the work prominently, turning the personification of recorded glory into a vehicle for her own claim on artistic posterity.

artworks.title: Clio, Muse of History
artworks.description: The Roman painter Giovanni Baglione, a contemporary and rival of Caravaggio, depicts Kleio as a half-length figure absorbed in the act of writing, an open book and the rolled papyri of her capsa close at hand. Bathed in the dramatic chiaroscuro of early Seicento Rome, the Muse leans into her task with quiet intensity, her attributes — the scroll and the volume of records — marking her as the daughter of Memory who safeguards the chronicle of mortal and divine deeds for future ages.
